questions.ask: Look at the date on C066, the Swiss 5 francs. Does it end in 6 or in 8?
questions.why: The phone photo reads 1976 but the record says 1978. Only the coin can settle it.

questions.ask: How many stars are on token T001 (the 20 play token with GR)?
questions.why: Its record says 13 stars; its twin T002 has 15. If they differ they are two different kinds.

questions.ask: Turn over C153, the 2008 UK 10 pence. Does the back show a crowned lion, or a piece of the Royal Shield?
questions.why: 2008 had both designs. The record lists the lion type.

questions.ask: East Caribbean coins are filed under the code EC, which is really Ecuador's code. Switch East Caribbean to XC?
questions.why: It only changes the short code in serial numbers (EC-... to XC-...), before the one-time serial renumbering.

questions.ask: Before your first bullion buy on Sept 12, did you already have about 1.5 oz of silver with no record? (For example a 1/2 oz round, 1/4 oz rounds, or a 1.5 oz piece.)
questions.why: The silver total includes 1.5 oz that no bullion record explains.

questions.ask: Your Mercury dime album (A006): from your page photos it has 77 holes, but the record says about 80. Is 77 right?
questions.why: The 80 was an estimate. Only you can lower a count.

questions.ask: Do you have two UK 5 pence coins dated 1992?
questions.why: C169 (from the ledger) and C275 (added later from a photo) are both 1992 5p. They may be the same coin logged twice.

questions.ask: Please take a phone photo of C140's map side (Spain 2008 1 cent) and drop it in the STAGING folder.
questions.why: Spain's 1 cent changed design in 2010; the map side helps confirm the catalog number.
